title: Sunny and the Long Grass Sea | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the little quokka finds a wide moonlit meadow where the long grass ripples like a silver sea, and she lies down in it and lets the sound carry her gently to sleep. A dreamy, soothing bedtime story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The moon had risen, round and full, over the edge of the bush. Little Sunny the quokka had been following the path through the trees, and now she came to somewhere she had never been before — the edge of a wide, wide meadow.

The grass was long and pale, almost silver in the moonlight. And when the wind moved through it, the whole meadow moved too — a soft, slow wave that rolled from one side all the way to the other, just like the sea.

Sunny stood at the very edge and watched.

The grass rippled. Then settled. Then rippled again, from a new direction, another wave following the first.

The sound it made was very soft. A dry, gentle whisper — shhhh — as each wave moved through. Shhhh. And again. Shhhh. It was the sound of something breathing, slow and steady and content.

Sunny took a careful step into the grass. Then another. The long blades bent gently around her, and the world grew close and soft, the sound filling her ears from every side at once.

She lay down.

Around her the grass swayed slowly, and the shushing sound continued, and the whole meadow seemed to rock, very gently, like a boat on still water. Up and down. Just a little. Calm and steady.

The moon was bright above, and the stars were bright, and the grass was moving, and everything was soft.

Sunny closed her eyes.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, long grass sea. Goodnight, little one.
